artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: table-row source-line plumbing (parser->matcher->annotator), always-on roadmap-structure marker with two conditional loud banners and additive JSON fields, fixture-based end-to-end verification matrix, and the declared file_scope expansion surfacing the new signal in /review.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed roadmap-integration.sh silently reporting success while annotating nothing: table-row matches are now located via a plumbed line-index/raw_line/status_index reference and rewritten in place preserving pipe-table structure; the script always emits a machine-readable roadmap-structure marker plus loud unparseable/no-op banners and additive JSON fields (roadmap_structure, warnings, high_confidence_matches, silent_noop); and /review (the sole consumer) was extended, as a declared file_scope expansion, to extract, surface in the transcript and report, and disambiguate the new signal in its commit message.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell script must diagnose 'ran successfully but did nothing meaningful,' emit two complementary signals rather than one literal condition: an always-on machine-readable structure marker (e.g. `<!-- roadmap-structure phases=N checkboxes=M table_rows=T parseable=true|false -->`, mirroring literature-briefing.sh's `<!-- lit-coverage ... -->` convention) plus conditional loud bracketed banners, AND additive JSON fields (never stderr-only) when the payload's consumer parses specific fields rather than scanning transcripts. Split a naive single unparseable-condition check into two signals if a valid, fully-handleable input shape can otherwise coincide with the 'nothing recognized' shape (e.g. a table-only roadmap has phases==0 && checkboxes==0, identical to truly unparseable, unless a third count like table_rows is also checked).

When a script must locate and rewrite a specific line it parsed earlier (not just search for it again), capture a (line_index, raw_line) reference pair at parse time and use it -- never re-derive location from content text, which can collide across rows with identical text. Before writing, re-verify the on-disk line at that index still equals the captured raw_line; treat any mismatch as a recorded skip, never a blind write. This pattern generalizes beyond markdown table rows to any text-rewriting pipeline with a parse-then-annotate split.

A dry-run mode that increments a 'would succeed' counter without confirming the target actually exists over-reports success. Fix by gating the dry-run increment on the exact same existence/agreement check the real apply path performs, so dry-run and apply can never diverge on what counts as achievable.
